title: Technology Identification
objective: Run nikto with a narrowed tuning set that reduces the scan to information disclosure and software identification, and build an accurate technology stack picture of the local application from the evidence.
prerequisites: Exercise 01 completed and its preflight evidence saved.
Nikto is installed and on your PATH. Run nikto -Version and record the version.
OWASP Juice Shop is running on http://localhost:3001.
You have created the folder evidence/nikto/.
expected_observation: The lab maps --tuning 7b to nikto's tuning options 7 and b: option 7 retrieves server and software information, option b is software identification. The output should be far shorter than a default nikto run, and it should focus on things like the server header, the technology stack, known-interesting files for the detected product, and any information disclosure items. Against Juice Shop you should typically see disclosure of the underlying server/framework (for example an Express/Node.js style stack) and possibly items about files or endpoints that reveal the application type. Nothing here is a guaranteed vulnerability; nikto items are leads to investigate. Record exactly what you saw; do not assume a specific item count, and do not record an item you did not actually see.
student_task: Run the exact command above from the lab project root.
Read the whole nikto output and, for every line that ends with a 200 response code, write down what was retrieved.
Build a short technology stack list in your notes: product name, version if shown, and the evidence line that supports each entry.
Note the 'Target IP', 'Target Hostname' and 'Server' header lines that nikto reports and check them against your authorized scope.
Save the unmodified JSON output the lab produced to evidence/nikto/ex04-nikto-software.json and save your stack list to evidence/nikto/ex04-tech-stack.md.
evidence_requirement: File evidence/nikto/ex04-nikto-software.json containing the unmodified JSON output from this tuned run.
File evidence/nikto/ex04-tech-stack.md containing your technology stack list, each entry citing the nikto line that supports it.
A quoted Server header value and a statement confirming the reported target host and IP are localhost/loopback.
These filenames must be referenced in the evidence index of your final report (Exercise 12).

questions.question: What technology stack did nikto help you identify, and which specific pieces of evidence support each conclusion?
questions.guidance: Cite the exact header values or retrieved items, for example a Server or X-Powered-By style header, and the product-specific items nikto listed. Explain that fingerprinting narrows which advisories and misconfigurations are even plausible for this application.

questions.question: What does the tuning value 7b actually restrict, and what did it deliberately leave out compared with a default nikto run?
questions.guidance: Explain that 7 = server and software information retrieval and b = software identification, so this run is limited to fingerprinting and disclosure. Note that a default run would additionally attempt file upload checks, injection probes, remote file retrieval, denial-of-service style tests and similar categories, which this lab excludes on purpose because they are intrusive or unsafe.

questions.question: How should a report author treat a nikto item that returned HTTP 200?
questions.guidance: Explain that a 200 means the resource exists and is reachable, not that it is exploitable; the item is an unauthenticated-disclosure lead whose severity must be justified by what the resource actually contains. Remind yourself never to fetch or browse anything outside the authorized target while chasing the lead.

safety_note: Authorized local-only use against http://localhost:3001. The tuned run in this exercise is limited to information retrieval and software identification so that no intrusive probe category is enabled. Do not remove the tuning restriction, do not re-point nikto at any external host, public domain, or IP address, and do not add -h values for systems you do not own. Discovery must never be followed by exploitation, credential testing, data extraction, or denial-of-service activity.

checklist.label: I ran python -m bcssl run nikto --tuning 7b from the lab project root and kept the full console output.
I recorded the Target IP, Target Hostname and Server header lines nikto reported and verified they are the local authorized target.
I saved the unmodified JSON to evidence/nikto/ex04-nikto-software.json and wrote my evidence-cited stack list to evidence/nikto/ex04-tech-stack.md.
I explained what the 7b tuning restricts, classified every 200 item as a lead rather than a proven vulnerability, and answered q1, q2 and q3.
